cases.description: A minimal audit event hashes to its leaf digest under SHA-256(0x00 || JCS(event)).
The same event with its members in a different source order canonicalizes identically, so it pins the same leaf digest as minimal-event-accepts.
agentSignature is removed before canonicalizing, so attaching it does not change the leaf; this pins the same digest as minimal-event-accepts.
A nested object, an array, and a safe-integer number canonicalize and pin the leaf digest.
A non-ASCII string value is canonicalized with minimal JCS escaping and pins the leaf digest, exercising UTF-16 member handling.
An empty object is a valid event and hashes SHA-256(0x00 || "{}").
A JSON array is not an audit event object and is rejected.
A JSON string is not an audit event object and is rejected.
JSON null is not an audit event object and is rejected.
A lone UTF-16 surrogate escape in a value is rejected before hashing, because a parser that rewrote it to U+FFFD would commit different bytes.
A number past the safe-integer range (2^53) is rejected, so the leaf path enforces the same number profile as signing.
An event nested past the depth bound (32) is rejected before canonicalization, in both implementations, so neither commits a leaf the other refuses.
An event with more nodes than the bound (10000) is rejected before canonicalization, bounding the work a hostile event can force.
An event whose canonical body exceeds the 1 MiB cap is rejected after canonicalization, so a Go witness cannot commit a leaf the reference refuses to hash.
